title: Controv. IV: Whether God has a general or antecedent will to save all and each
pass_a_gloss: II. Whether there is in God a general Will, or antecedent, of saving all & each human beings; and the same not that which is called the will of the sign, by His word promiscuously signifying the way of salvation to any, inviting any without distinction to the recognition of the truth, 1 Tim. 2:4, but the will properly so called of God, or of good-pleasure, that eternal, serious, efficacious one; Yet not absolute or immutable, but ordered & conditioned, under the conditions of faith, & of perseverance to be performed by human beings?
pass_b_english: II. Is there in God a general will, or an antecedent will, to save all human beings and each one — and that not what is called the will of the sign, by which His word promiscuously marks the way of salvation for any, inviting any without distinction to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4), but God's will properly so called, the will of His good-pleasure: that eternal, serious, efficacious will — yet not absolute or immutable, but ordered and conditioned, under the conditions of faith and of perseverance that human beings are to perform?
source_text: II. An sit in Deo Voluntas generalis, seu antecedens, servandi omnes & singulos homines; eademque non quae dicitur voluntas signi, verbo suo quibusvis promiscuè viam salutis significans, quosvis sine discrimine invitans ad agnitionem veritatis, 1. Tim. II. 4. sed voluntas propriè dicta Dei, seu beneplaciti, aeterna illa, seria, efficax; Nec absoluta tamen aut immutabilis, sed ordinata & conditionata, sub conditionibus fidei, & perseverantiae ab hominibus praestandae?
